title: The work list
dek: What is being done here, as opposed to what is known.
lead: Every other register in this archive answers what it knows. **What has been read** carries the negatives, **Open questions** carries what is unanswered, **Corrections** carries what it got wrong. None of them answered what is actually being *done*, so that lived in a chat window — and on 15 September a whole day went into re-reading two registers that `notes/` already recorded as swept, because the thing that knew was a conversation and conversations end. This page is the register that outlives the session. **The rows are in the order they would be done** — finish what is started, then what is cheapest against what it settles, then what is expensive but unavoidable, and last what is waiting on somebody outside this archive.
close: Nothing here is a research finding. Those belong on [What has been read](/searched/), [Open questions](/open-questions/) and [Corrections](/corrections/). This list answers one question only: **who has to move it next.**

rows.what: Read the Arienzo death indexes, 1831–1843
rows.note:
**Done 15 September.** Thirteen annual volumes, 55 images, scanned by cropping the surname column from every page and tiling them eight to a sheet. **Two new children** — Pasquale Falco (1838) and Matteo Falco (1842) — **five empty years**, four years already held, and **one year that is not a negative**: the 1834 index is a single leaf covering A to C and marked END. 

This did **not** close Antonia di Guida's death or Pasqua Falco, which is what it was picked up for. Neither is in the stretch, so both move to the register itself.

rows.what: Verify three index readings deliberately left unpublished
rows.note:
**Done 15 September.** All three magnified and settled. Two are real children and are published: a **second Giuseppe Cioffi** (5 Dec 1830) and a **second Mariantonia Cioffi** (3 Dec 1832), which brings that household to **six children buried in nine years**, none known to have reached adulthood. 

The third is a **conflict left open on purpose**: the index says «Morgillo Raffaela, 9 Marzo 1832», the act already held says «Raffaele Morgillo, 22, contadino, 9 May 1832». Two children nine weeks apart, or one death read two ways. **Reading atto 14 of 1832 against the held act settles it** — that is now the work, and it is small.

rows.what: Giuseppe Falco's death, 1859 onward — and Vincenzo's in the same reading
rows.note:
**DONE, and the answer is that the record is out of reach — which is an answer.** **1865 (`an_ua14367`) read end to end: 147 acts, no Falco death.** The Antenati Arienzo death series stops there.

**VINCENZO FALCO was ALIVE on 16 December 1864**, named without «fu» in his son Luigi's death act, a *colono* still on strada Camellara at seventy-two. **So his death is 1866 or later**, in the post-Unification *Stato civile italiano* this archive has never located for Arienzo. The months of searching 1844–1865 were not wasted: they are what proves it.

**GIUSEPPE FALCO of Antonia di Guida** is in the same position — alive November 1849, and in none of 1850–1859 or 1865. See rows 39 and 40, which now share one answer.

rows.what: Find the finding aid for Arienzo marriages after 1849
rows.note:
**Answered 15 September: the register is the finding aid.** The «Matrimoni, indice» series stops at 1849, but the **Matrimoni registers run on** at `an_ua14213` + (year − 1809) — 28 to 37 acts a year, each an «atto di solenne promessa» naming **both spouses, both sets of parents, and the parish celebration date in the margin**. Small enough to read outright. 

The first volume opened produced **Sara Falco's marriage** (14 Feb 1855, to Antonio Mauro, fruttajolo). **Nunziata is not in it**, which is now its own question on the searched page. Antonio Falco's 1869 marriage is beyond this series, which ends with the Restoration in 1865.

rows.what: Sara Falco's parish baptism
rows.note:
**The lead is confirmed and the baptism is still unread.** The cached index leaf (`3Q9M-CSD3-1325-9`) reads «**Sara Falco fol. 47**» — an alphabetical index by FORENAME, so she sits in the S run beside Salvatore, Sabbatino and Saverio. **Reading folio 47 needs the image**, which depends on row 18. 

The search for her turned up something else entirely: **SARA RUGGIERO, her grandmother, as MATRINA on ten pages across six Falco households** — published, at transcript strength. Eight of the nine 'Sara' hits in the harvest were the grandmother, not the granddaughter.

rows.what: Arcangelo Crisci — one man or two?
rows.note:
**Done 15 September — two men.** The 1817 birth register holds both: Arcangelo Crisci **52**, strada Camellara, husband of **Sara Ruggiero**; and Arcangelo Crisci **30**, strada Capodiconca, husband of **Maria Martone**. Twenty-two years, two streets, two wives. **Andreana's father is not Anna Falco's husband.** 

Both ages were already in `data/sweep-people.tsv` and had been for weeks. 

**A smaller question opened:** Anna's husband is son of «fu Nicola, e Chiara Majone», and the younger Arcangelo was married to Maria Martone in 1817 — so either he remarried within months or there is a third man of the name.

rows.what: Test whether Giuseppe Nunzio and Nunziata carry one family name
rows.note:
**Done 15 September — and the answer is no.** Nunziata Falco is not in the Arienzo marriage registers for **1854, 1855 or 1856**, all read act by act. She is held here from a parish record as marrying «13 [Nov] 1855», the month in brackets. Either that date is wrong or she married at her husband's comune. **Nothing connects her to Giuseppe Nunzio beyond the shared root of the name**, and this archive is not going to build on that. 

The sweep found other things instead: **Pasqua Falco's marriage** (9 Sep 1856), which vindicated a refusal; **Giuseppe Falco of strada Costa remarrying** in 1854 with his parents named; and **Gelsomina Vigliotta dead before December 1854**, stated twice.

rows.what: Audit the 180 corrections entries for ones now superseded
rows.note: **Done. 192 entries read end to end; nineteen were still asserting something a later finding had overturned**, eleven of them still labelled `open`. Each now carries the entry that replaced it, named and linked, above its own text. **The structural cause was on the page in plain sight**: a withdrawal was published as a new entry at the top, and the page sorts by date, so it sat sixty rows from the claim it killed. Three further faults fell out — a forty-volume negative run against a retired surname, a duplicate discovery of an entry on this very page, and the page printing its own markdown for a week.

rows.what: Birth tavole 1818–1820, 1829 onward, and 1845–1860 for Giovanna Arricale's siblings
rows.note:
**1819 is done** — 137 acts, act by act, because the volume has **no annual tavola** (both ends checked; the twenty-one-row list on the last leaf is a supplementary list, not the year's index). **Three Falco births, all on strada Camellara**: Domenico Clemente (18 Mar), **Crescenzo — a birth date for a man held by his marriages alone** (11 Oct), and Luigi's civil act (21 Dec). **Rosaria Falco is not in it either**, which closes the last year her birth act could have been in. **Next: 1820** (`an_ua14417`, 143 images) — still hunting **Maria Rosa Falco**, absent from 1817, 1818 and 1819. Then 1829 onward and 1845–1860.

**16 September — the tavole are NOT there for the years that matter.** **1829** (`an_ua14426`, 114 images, **107 acts**) has **no tavola at either end**: image 2 is act 1, image 113 the closing certificate, image 114 the Procuratore's. **1837** (`an_ua14434`, 146 images) likewise — image 2 is act 1. The archival tag «*THIS INDEX HAS BEEN MICROFILMED ALREADY*» on the 1829 endpapers refers to a separately filmed index, **not** to anything bound in.

**So 1829 onward is an act-by-act read at roughly one act per leaf**, and the one-image-per-year economy that made 1828, 1848 and 1859 cheap does not apply. **1830 is 149 images, 1837 is 146.** Budget accordingly; the sheets must be three columns wide to carry a negative, not four.

rows.what: Find the second filming of the 1825 birth tavola
rows.note:
The 1825 index leaf is **covered by an inserted sheet** in the filming held here, and the photographer's own card lies across the frame reading *THIS INDEX HAS BEEN MICROFILMED ALREADY*. So it exists. The method that found Gioacchino's 1779 baptism — regexing already-cached transcripts for a duplicate shoot — is the way in.

**16 September — IT IS NOT JUST 1825.** The **1846** birth volume (`an_ua14443`, img 109) carries **the same card, in the same hand**: «*THIS INDEX HAS BEEN MICROFILMED ALREADY*», laid across the tavola leaf, with the whole index showing through mirrored from the verso and nothing readable. **Two volumes twenty-one years apart, one policy.** So this row is not about recovering a single leaf — **the Arienzo birth tavole were filmed as a separate series and that series has never been located.** Finding it would hand this archive an every-year index to the births, which is the instrument it has been sweeping ninety acts at a time to do without. **Raise the priority accordingly.**

**17 September — ONE PLACE RULED OUT, AND IT WAS WORTH RULING OUT.** The `an_ua140xx` ark block, which sits just below the marriage-index block and looked like a candidate for a separate index filming, **is not the tavole.** It is the **«Diversi»** series — «*Atti per le nascite avvenuti in un viaggio di mare, Per le Ricognizioni, Adozioni, **Persone defunte e fuori del proprio domicilio**, e Morti-Nati*» — and it turned out to be a seam of its own. **See the new row.** The birth tavole are still unlocated.

rows.what: Where is Sant'Agnese?
rows.note:
Generation four's marriage act names «*Josaphat Ruggiero, parroco di **Sant'Agnese***» and makes the bride his parishioner; the civil act, found the same day, says she was **born and still domiciled at San Felice a Cancello**. This archive has been calling Sant'Agnese one of Arienzo's three parishes on the strength of **the film the act sits in** — and a film label covers a whole reel. One rate window: re-read the act for its own words for the place.

**17 September — EVIDENCE, NOT AN ANSWER.** Two marriages on ONE leaf of the **Sant'Andrea** register, June 1820, each marry a bride the writer calls «*meam Parochianam*» to a groom «***ex Parrocchia SANCTAE AGNETIS***» — Gennaro Solli to Angela Grassia on 31 May, and Angelo Clemente Frasca to Angela Rosa Crisci on 1 June. **Two men from Sant'Agnese marrying into Sant'Andrea inside two days** is the behaviour of a parish next door, not one in another town. **It is still not the act saying where Sant'Agnese IS**, which is what this row asked for — but it is the first evidence that does not come from a film label. **Both leaves also date the diocese: «*decreto Episcopalis Curiae SANCTAE AGATHAE GOTHORUM*» — Arienzo answered to Sant'Agata de' Goti**, which is where a diocesan archive would hold what the parish does not.

rows.what: Explain why the 1841 civil register holds no Falco death
rows.note:
**DONE 16 Sep 2026 — THE REGISTER ANSWERS IT ITSELF, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT IT IS NOT CONTINUOUS.**

**Test 1, the numbering gap: there is none.** Acts **78 to 91 run unbroken**, read from the image. And the volume ends at **91**, not ninety — this archive's own statement «*all ninety acts*» was one act short.

**Test 2, a supplementary list at the back: cannot be run on this filming.** There is a tavola leaf after the last act (`an_ua14343` img 55 left), but it is photographed with its ink almost wholly lost and the facing page's writing transferred onto it in mirror. Three order-numbers survive and no names. **Not read, and not recorded as absent.**

**Test 3 is the one that answers the question. THE DEATH DATES HAVE AN ELEVEN-DAY HOLE, AND THE FALCO BURIAL IS INSIDE IT.** Read act by act from the image, the deaths run: **act 84 — 19 November · act 85 — 23 November · act 86 — 26 November · act 87 — 7 DECEMBER.** **The comune registered nothing between 26 November and 7 December 1841. The parish buried JOANNES FALCO on 27 November.**

**And the hole is not special, which is the real finding.** A fortnight earlier the register does it again: **act 80 is a death of 30 October and act 81 a death of 13 November — fourteen days.** Two silences of a fortnight and eleven days in one autumn, in a register that otherwise enters a death every two or three days that season. **This register was not capturing every death at Arienzo**, and its own date sequence proves it without any inference from the parish book.

**So the 1841 civil nil for Falco is not evidence of anything** — and neither is any other nil taken from this volume without checking the dates either side of it. Rows 12 and 56 are the same question and both close here.

rows.what: Promote the harvested files into households
rows.note:
**Done — and the row was measuring the wrong thing, which is the finding.** «Promote the harvested files into households» assumed the backlog was people without a household. It is not: **764 of the 1,087 valle-caudina rows have no household, and they should not have one** — they are the Falco of Paolisi and Moiano, whom this archive has never claimed as kin. **Giving them a household would be a claim, not a promotion.**

**Measured properly across every research file: 23,741 named rows, of which all but 128 already reach the register and the search index.** The harvests are not stranded. 

**But THREE files reached the site not at all** — `falco-baptisms-parsed.tsv` (48), `arricale-from-transcripts.tsv` (18) and `falco-parentage.tsv` (22). **Eighty-eight rows, invisible and unfindable for as long as they have existed**, including the Arienzo parish baptisms whose blank names were row 57's subject. **All three are now in `build_register.py`, marked as MACHINE READINGS of mangled Latin** so nobody mistakes a parsed spelling for a transcription.

rows.what: Moiano and Paolisi — never examined
rows.note:
**Moiano** is the second stronghold of both Zampiello (104 records) and Annecchino (215). **Paolisi** is where Francesco Falco came from in 1714, and where the Giovanna Falco found this week married a Lettieri. Neither town has ever been opened.

**COUNTED, 15 September:** `data/antenati-valle-caudina.tsv` holds **406 Falco at Paolisi and 310 at Moiano**, plus 215 Annecchino and 104 Zampiello at Moiano. **All of them reach the register and are searchable**; none is claimed as kin. **The row is not about making them reachable — it is about deciding whether any of them belongs to this family**, which is a reading job on 1,087 rows and has never been started.

rows.what: The eighteenth-century parish marriage register
rows.note: Two things sit in it. **Matteo Falco's own marriage**, which would name his father and break the line's frontier; and the **Maria Falco × Francesco Cioffi** marriage, which the civil series cannot hold because the Arienzo civil registers begin in 1809 and that marriage is older than they are.

rows.what: Maddalena Falco's baptism — two passes spent, still unread
rows.note:
**DONE 17 Sep 2026 — and the two failed passes failed because this row had the wrong leaf.**

«*[Anno] D[omi]ni **1818**, die vero **septima 7 Junii**, R[everendu]s D. **BLASIUS MANSIONARIUS ARRICALE** Substitutus baptizavit infantem **natam** ex **JOSEPHO FALCO et ANTONIA DI GUIDA** conjugibus hujus Parochiae, **cui dedit nomen MAGDALENA. Matrina fuit DOROTHEA D'ADDIO.** HYACINTHUS Archip. MORGILLO*»

**Same day as her civil birth act**, and **the godmother is the same Dorotea d'Addio who stood at Gioacchino Falco's font in 1779** — one woman at this family's baptisms across forty years.

**THE ARK IN THIS ROW IS THE INDEX LEAF, NOT THE ACT.** `3Q9M-CSD3-1381-R` carries the **margin label** «Maddalena Falco», which is what both rendering passes went hunting and found. **The act is on `3Q9M-CSD3-13LG-7`.** In this parish register the year's index and the year's acts are on different leaves, and a search that lands on the label will never reach the entry however many tiles it renders.

**Found by full-text rather than by rendering**, with the quoted phrase «Maddalena Falco» — two hits in the whole baptism collection, one the label and one the act. **Machine transcription; the image is not yet read.**

rows.what: Two tool bugs that may exist in every sibling archive
rows.note: Both were found here and **neither is peculiar to this archive**. First: the person-graph builder cleans names to keep old URLs alive, and that cleaning **strips brackets before comparing them** — which cost this archive an entire generation of its own direct line, because `line.json` spelt a wife «Adriana (Andreana) Crisci» and every act spells her ANDREANA. Second: the search index indexed `404.astro`, which Astro emits as `404.html` and never as a page, so the archive check failed on a row pointing at a page that is never built. **Any archive sharing these tools has both.** **A THIRD, FOUND 15 SEPTEMBER: `WorkList.astro`'s markdown renderer drops code spans and mis-pairs bold.** Its `md()` handles `&`, `<`, links, `**bold**` and «guillemets» — **but not backticks**, so every ark number in a note (`an_ua14362`) renders with its backticks showing. **This page has forty-six of them.** **And its bold is `\*\*([^*]+)\*\*`** — the greedy no-nested-italic form. On «**San Felice a Cancello, *Matrimoni* 1844**», the common shape in these archives, it mis-pairs across the inner italic and nests the tags wrongly. **Both are fixed in this archive's own `site/src/lib/md.js`** — non-greedy `[\s\S]+?` bold, then italics, then code — and the fix is four lines. **Every sibling archive using WorkList with ark numbers in its notes has this.** **17 September — MEASURED, TESTED, AND ONE SENTENCE ABOVE IS WRONG.** **The blast radius, on this page.** Of **70 rows**, **42 contain backticks** — **148 code spans**, and the built page renders **296 literal backtick characters and not one `` tag**. There are also **57 single-asterisk italics**, and the kit's renderer **has no italic rule at all**, so every one of those shows its asterisks too. **The second bug is worse than this row said.** This row claimed the greedy `\*\*([^*]+)\*\*` «*mis-pairs across the inner italic and nests the tags wrongly*». **It does not mis-pair. It cannot match at all**, because `[^*]` refuses to cross the inner `*` — so the whole span renders as literal asterisks and the bold simply does not happen. Three spans on this page are in that state. **Run against both renderers rather than reasoned about:** ``` IN ANTENATI `an_ua14362`, 55 images kit ANTENATI `an_ua14362`, 55 images new ANTENATI an_ua14362, 55 images IN **San Felice a Cancello, *Matrimoni* 1844** kit **San Felice a Cancello, *Matrimoni* 1844** new San Felice a Cancello, Matrimoni 1844 ``` **THE PATCH, PROVEN.** Replace the bold line in `kit/components/WorkList.astro` and add two rules after it — the order matters, bold before italics before code: ```js .replace(/\*\*([\s\S]+?)\*\*/g, "$1") .replace(/\*([^*\n]+)\*/g, "$1") .replace(/`([^`]+)`/g, "$1") ``` That is this archive's `site/src/lib/md.js` exactly, and the three cases above are its test. **NOT APPLIED FROM HERE, DELIBERATELY.** `@daviddef/archive-kit` is a separate repository pinned by commit in `site/package.json`, another session owns the shared kit, and **every one of the seven archives renders its work list through this component**. The patch is four lines and it is written out above so whoever owns the kit can apply it without rediscovering any of this.

rows.what: Read the FamilySearch image behind a machine transcript
rows.note:
**ONE SIGN-IN UNBLOCKS THIS, and the reason changed on 16 September.** The note used to say the blocker was the desktop Browser pane not being displayed. **It is not that.** FindMyPast signs in fine in the browser context this session drives — twelve surnames were swept through it today. **FamilySearch specifically has no session there**: `/en/tree/find` redirects to `/en/search/tree/`, `/en/home/` to `/en/australia/`, and every image ark bounces to `ident.familysearch.org`. Those are the signed-out paths. **A tab is parked on the target ark**; signing in *in that tab* — not a new window — puts the session where this session can use it. **Credentials are David's to enter and will not be entered here.**

**THE TARGET: `3:1:3Q9M-CSD3-13CP-B`**, whose snippet opens «*Raphael Falco **Obiit die 26 Februarii 18[8]1***». **RAFFAELE FALCO, GENERATION FOUR, HAS NO DEATH IN THIS ARCHIVE.** Born 10 May 1818, he would be **sixty-two** in February 1881, and this is the only candidate ever seen.

**The OCR gives the year as «1811» twice while the harvest's own metadata says 1881** — and eight and one are the two digits this engine confuses most. **If 1811, a stranger born before generation four. If 1881, very likely him.** One image decides it.

**Also waiting on the same sign-in:** row 5 (Sara Falco's parish baptism, folio 47 of `3Q9M-CSD3-1325-9`), row 16 (Maddalena Falco's baptism, `3Q9M-CSD3-1381-R`), and **43 parish-baptism snippets** whose child's name falls outside the 260-character window.

rows.what: The National Archives of Australia files
rows.note: **J25 1971/9830** and **J25 1972/4964** — Brisbane immigration case files, paper only, not digitised. Files of this era normally carry the sponsor, the addresses, the occupations and often photographs, and 1972/4964 is already marked Open. There are also **three NAA passenger images** whose transcripts give a name, a year and nothing else. Anyone can order copies.

rows.what: The restricted Caserta images, and the Museo Alfonsiano
rows.note: Several Caserta record images return *«This record can only be displayed on certain accounts»* — the index and machine transcripts are open, the scans are not. **A visit to a FamilySearch centre or an affiliate library unlocks them.** Separately, the **Museo Alfonsiano** stands in the old bishop's palace beside Sant'Andrea, the church this family was baptised in for two centuries, and may hold or know of parish material that was never filmed. That needs a letter or a visit.

rows.what: The two un-scanned Benevento volumes
rows.note: **Arpaia births 1895** and **Forchia births 1897** are not digitised — first inferred from ark arithmetic, since the shelf-marks run consecutively and skip those years, and since confirmed. They are what still blocks Filomena Annecchino's birth. Ordering or reading them at the Archivio di Stato di Benevento is the only route.

rows.what: The processetti — 378 volumes across six towns
rows.note: Marriage supplement files: birth extracts, parental consents, death certificates of parents already dead. **One file can carry two generations backwards.** None have been read. This is the largest unworked seam in the project and it needs time rather than a decision. **Re-counted 15 September: 378 volumes across SIX towns, not 258 across four.** San Felice a Cancello was not surveyed until 13 September and carries 57 on its own; Arienzo holds 43 with zero name-indexed records. **Three towns are still completely unexamined — Moiano, Paolisi and San Felice a Cancello, 199 volumes between them** — and this row now covers exactly those three, so retiring one lowers the backlog by one.

rows.what: Ancestry for the Australian end — MyHeritage is already harvested, FindMyPast is now open
rows.note:
**Partly unblocked on 16 September, and the row was overstating it.** **MyHeritage is NOT blocked** — this archive already harvests it: `data/myheritage-facts.tsv` holds **427 rows**, and the family tree itself lives there. **FindMyPast is now open** on a one-month subscription David started on 16 September; that work is row 65, running.

**What is genuinely left is ANCESTRY**, for the Brisbane generations' passenger lists and naturalisation files. No subscription, and nothing here can move it. **Before buying one, read row 65's result**: FindMyPast's Australian holding for this family turned out to be six passenger records and the Italian sets are the FamilySearch index re-hosted. **Ancestry may be the same trade twice**, and the thing actually worth paying for is probably the NAA files in row 19, which anyone can order for a copying fee.

rows.what: DNA matches on the Falco and Zampiello sides
rows.note: Matches could confirm or break the Annecchino descent, and could find living cousins in Campania. **No register can do that.** The family already has tests in play; the matches need working through.

rows.what: FreeBMD, RootsChat and Arcanum — deliberately not searched
rows.note: **A decision, recorded so nobody spends a day rediscovering it.** This family has no English and no Habsburg generations. All three are wrong for it, and saying so on [What has been read](/searched/) is worth more than searching them would have been.

rows.what: Re-reading registers that notes/ already recorded as swept
rows.note: **Founded on a mistake, kept rather than deleted.** A day went into reading the 1816 and 1817 birth registers and into deriving the trap that these forms carry a *printed* year the clerk strikes and corrects by hand. Both were already written up in `notes/1817-birth-register-progress.md`, which says *«Result: no Falco at all»* and, in its second line, *«every act is pre-printed sedici and corrected by hand to diciassette»*. The negatives stand and were already this archive's negatives. **The standing rule now is to read `notes/QUEUE.md` and the 83 per-year progress files before opening any register.**

rows.what: Re-read the Arienzo marriage indexes 1809–1849 for FALCO × CIOFFI
rows.note: **STRUCK — founded on a mistake, and kept here rather than deleted.** The audit read the corrections page's prose, saw the retired surname «Cossi», and concluded forty volumes had been searched for the wrong man. **They were searched for the bride.** The *What has been read* record lists, year by year, where no FALCO married at Arienzo, and reports thirteen Falco marriages found — a reader in the F section of a tavola sees a Maria Falco whoever she marries. **The negative stands and the marriage is pre-1809**, as `notes/QUEUE.md` already said, with the surname already correct. What was real was a wrong name in the prose, now fixed.

rows.what: Re-render the two strada Camellara declarants at 8× and apply the three-way test
rows.note: **Done. CIOFFI.** Arienzo *Morti 1843* atto 43, read at magnification: «*LUCA CIOFFI di anni trentatré, Sartore … e GIOVANNI CIOFFI di anni quarantatré, contadino*», both of strada Camellara. The *ff* ligature — two tall ascenders and a long descender — settles it, exactly as the withdrawn correction's own method note described before reading it backwards. **The withdrawn correction had the AGES right and the household file did not** (it carried 48 for Giovanni, the act says 43). Two records of one act, each holding half of it, disagreeing for two days. Both now fixed.

rows.what: Audit the corrections page again when it passes 250 entries
rows.note: **192 entries took one pass and produced five findings.** The page is appended to daily and read back never — which is how nineteen entries came to be standing after the finding that killed them. **Recurring, not one-off**, because the failure is structural: the page grows at the top and nobody walks down it.

rows.what: A check that a new finding is not already published
rows.note:
**Done: `tools/isitnew.py`.** One command, every corpus, before the write-up — corrections, work list, both household files, people, register, the searched page and all eighty-odd progress notes. Each argument is searched independently and it prints where the term already appears.

**Tested against the failure it exists for.** `python3 tools/isitnew.py "FALCO CARMELA"` returns hits in the corrections, the household file, people AND the register — **the 1859 duplication would have been stopped before a word of it was written.**

**Deliberately not a build gate.** It cannot know whether a hit means the finding is old; it is a lookup, not a judgement. What it removes is the excuse: **a hit is not proof the finding is old and a miss is not proof it is new — it means nobody can say they did not look.**

rows.what: Look for Nunziata Falco's marriage in the MARGIN of her birth act
rows.note:
**A birth act can carry a marriage, and this archive only learned that today.** Act 33 of 1819 has the registrar's later note across its foot: «*Con atto 6 agosto 1856 atto 21 in S. Maria a Vico il Falco sposò Domenica Vigliotti*» — **a wedding in another comune, recorded nowhere an Arienzo marriage register would show it.** Work-list row 7 closed with Nunziata Falco absent from the Arienzo marriage registers of 1854, 1855 and 1856, all read act by act. **That absence now has a second possible explanation and a way to test it.** First find her birth act, then read its margin.

**PROMOTED by the pattern found on 15 September.** The annotation practice appears to begin between 1845 and 1856 — absent on marriages of 1844 and 1845, present on 1856 and 1880. **Nunziata married on 13 November 1855, which is exactly on that boundary.** Her margin is now the most informative one in the archive either way: it either gives her marriage, or it dates the practice to after November 1855.

**A SECOND ROUTE, 16 September.** The marriage volumes carry a **NOTIFICAZIONI register bound in after the acts** — banns, published where the couple lives even when the wedding is celebrated elsewhere. **That is this row's exact shape.** See the new banns row.

rows.what: Read the given name of act 99 of 1819 from a third source
rows.note:

rows.what: The Arienzo MARRIAGE REGISTERS after 1849 — there is no index at all

rows.what: ANTONIA DI GUIDA'S DEATH — the window has moved and the old negative may not cover it
rows.note:
**She is alive on 2 February 1845**, stated on a form that marks the dead explicitly. That is twenty-five years later than the only other dated document this archive had for her. **The existing negative was built when her window opened in 1819**: 229 Arienzo pages of the parish death register, searched on «Guida». The Arienzo CIVIL death registers are read act by act for **1844–1858** and **1859** — so if she died at Arienzo before 1860 she should already have been seen, and she was not. **That is now a real conflict rather than a gap**, and the candidates are: she died 1860–1865 (row 3's volumes), she died after 1865 where Antenati stops, she died at Santa Maria a Vico or another comune, or **she was missed in a sweep that was not looking for her.** Re-read the 1845–1858 F and G leaves with her name as the target.

**16 September: the series is exhausted.** **1865 is now read — 147 acts, no Falco.** Antenati's Arienzo deaths stop at 1865, and **Vincenzo Falco was demonstrably alive in December 1864**, which shows the series simply does not reach this generation's deaths. **The remaining years of 1860–1863 are still worth reading** for other Falco, but the answer for these two is almost certainly the same: **1866 or later, in a series this archive has not located.** Locating it is now the higher-value task.

**20 September — THE «DIVERSI» REGISTER IS READ OUT, AND THE ANSWER IS NO.** Work-list row 70 has now read **all 45 volumes, 1812–1865**, of the Arienzo register of **people who died away from home** — the one instrument that could have held a death this town never recorded. **Every act from 1845 to 1865 is read and its dead are named, and there is no FALCO and no DI GUIDA among them.** The only unnamed acts left in the series are four, all **before 1845**, so none can be this person.

**So the third explanation is spent.** A death missing from the Arienzo register is not explained here by the person having died elsewhere. **What remains is 1866 or later**, in the post-Unification registers this archive has still not located — or a comune whose own register was never transmitted to Arienzo at all.

rows.what: LUIGI FALCO, 1819–1864 — a life of forty-five years with no marriage in it
rows.note:
**DONE. He was married — to CAROLINA CIMMINO.** His death act, read from the image (it was a FamilySearch index stub): «*è morto nella sua casa **LUIGI FALCO = MARITO DI CAROLINA CIMMINO** — di anni quarantuno, di professione **industriante**, domiciliato **Contrada Capodiconca***». **He had left strada Camellara**, and his stated age is wrong by three — forty-one for a man five days short of forty-five.

**And the act answered a far older question in its parentage clause**: his parents are given with domiciles and **no «fu»**, in a register that marks four other dead parents on the same opening. **Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci were alive on 16 December 1864.**

**What remains of this row:** Carolina Cimmino. The Arienzo marriage record is complete 1809–1858 and holds no Falco–Cimmino, so **they married after 1858 or not at Arienzo.**

rows.what: ROSARIA FALCO's birth act — every Arienzo year has now been read and she is in none
rows.note:
**She died 15 March 1819, eleven hours after her brother, as a daughter of Giuseppe Falco and Gelsomina Vigliotta.** The Arienzo civil birth registers for **1816, 1817, 1818 and 1819** are all read end to end and she is in none of them. **A child dead in March 1819 was born in one of those years.** So either the act was never drawn, or **she was not born at Arienzo** — and this household is the one that turns up at **strada Costa**, then strada Camellara, then Santa Maria a Vico. Test the parish baptisms first, then Santa Maria a Vico.

**17 September — THE PARISH TEST WAS RUN AND IT CANNOT PRODUCE A NEGATIVE. Here is the proof.**

FamilySearch's full text of the Arienzo parish baptisms was searched for the Latin forms the clerk actually writes. **«*ex Josepho Falco*» returns TWO pages in the entire collection** — for a household with at least eight children — and Rosaria is not among them.

**That is not evidence of absence, because the machine cannot read the surname.** Measured on the same collection, same place filter:

| spelling | pages |
|---|---|
| `Falco` | **361** |
| `Falo` | **126** |
| `Falio` | **92** |
| `Zalco` | 7 |
| `Salco` | 6 |
| `Talco` | 3 |

**Two hundred and eighteen pages render the name in a form a search for «Falco» never sees — about a third of the corpus.** And one index leaf writes the SAME entry twice, once as «*Joseph Zalco fol: 185*» and once as «*Joseph Falco fol: 185*». **A surname phrase search here is a finding aid, never a negative.**

**What the test did turn up**: Maddalena Falco's baptism of 7 June 1818 (row 16), the day of Matteo's 1807 baptism, and **Domenico Clemente's baptism of 18 March 1819 — three days after this household buried Domenico and Rosaria eleven hours apart.** Rosaria's own act is still not found, and **Santa Maria a Vico is still untried.**

rows.what: CRESCENZO FALCO and Angela Maria Morgillo — their children
rows.note:
**A household created on 3 February 1845 and completely unexamined.** He was a *colono* of **strada Sant'Andrea**, twenty-five; she was twenty-three and an orphan. Their children would be in the Arienzo birth registers from late 1845 — which row 9 reaches but has never opened. **The tree already carries a «Crescenzo Falco» with a wife «Maria Concetta Morgillo» and a son Giovanni**, unsourced. That is either this marriage under a different forename for the bride, or a second couple. **A single birth act would decide it.**

**16 September — 1846 READ END TO END, AND CRESCENZO IS NOT IN IT.** All 110 images of `an_ua14443` swept on the «*è comparso*» band, plus the last two months of 1845 (`an_ua14442`, images 118–135), which is the window a first child of a February 1845 wedding would fall in. **Three Falco fathers in the two sweeps, none of them Crescenzo**: **MICHELE FALCO, 38, strada Camellara** (December 1845), **FRANCESCO FALCO, 42, strada Camellara** (January 1846) and **MATTEO FALCO, 38, colono, strada Camellara** (September 1846).

**Same caveat as every sweep of this kind**: the declarant line was read, and a large minority of these acts are declared by a **levatrice** — Leontina Martone, Rosa Morgillo, Felicia Martone recur — whose acts name the father lower down. **This does not close 1846; it makes Crescenzo unlikely in it.**

**And there is no index to check the sweep against.** The **1845** tavola is printed and **left blank**. The **1846** tavola exists but the camera skipped it, laying the operator's own card across the frame: «*THIS INDEX HAS BEEN MICROFILMED ALREADY*» — **the same card row 10 found over the 1825 leaf.** So it is not one lost index, it is a policy.

**Next: 1847 onward**, and the tree's rival «Crescenzo Falco × Maria Concetta Morgillo with a son Giovanni» is still undecided.

rows.what: The household of GENNARO MORGILLO and MARIA FELICIA SANSONE
rows.note:
**Done. The household exists.** **GENNARO MORGILLO**, *colono*, and **MARIA FELICIA SANSONE**, *contadina* — **both dead before 2 February 1845**, stated in their daughter's marriage act, which marks the dead explicitly. Their daughter **ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO**, twenty-three and an orphan, married Crescenzo Falco.

**SANSONE had never appeared in this archive at all.** Not claimed as kin; recorded because the Falco married the Morgillo repeatedly and this archive still cannot tell those Morgillo houses apart.

rows.what: SARA RUGGIERO — who she was, beyond a godmother's name
rows.note:
**DONE 17 Sep 2026 — she has a wedding, a father, a death window and two more children.**

**THE MARRIAGE.** «*Anno D[omi]ni … **1793**, die vero **vigesima sexta 26 Martii** … in matrimonio conjunxit nondum uxoratos **ARCHANGELUM CRISCI FILIUM NICOLAI**, et **SARAM RUGGIERO FILIAM PASCHALIS**, utrosque hujus Archipresbyteralis [Ecclesiae] **S. Andreae***» — Arienzo, **26 March 1793**, before D. Joseph Crisci, coadjutor, by decree of the episcopal curia of **Sant'Agata de' Goti**. He was about twenty-eight, she about twenty-one, and **Andreana Crisci — generation three's wife — was baptised three and a half years later.**

**HER FATHER: PASQUALE RUGGIERO**, living in March 1793. His is the name this row existed to find. **And the groom's father, NICOLA CRISCI**, a generation this archive did not have.

**A DEATH WINDOW OF THREE YEARS, where there was none.** She bore a son in **1817** aged forty-five, and by **1 June 1820** her daughter's marriage act writes «*q[uonda]m Sara Ruggiero*». **Dead between 1817 and June 1820, aged about forty-five to forty-eight.**

**AND TWO CHILDREN.** **ANGELA ROSA CRISCI**, married **1 June 1820** to Angelo Clemente Frasca of the parish of **Sant'Agnese**; and **LORENZO CRISCI**, married **25 March 1846** to Maria Angelica Ruotolo, daughter of Antonio and **Maria Giovanna CARFORA**.

**THE IDENTIFICATION RESTS ON THE COUPLE, NOT THE FORENAME** — this archive holds a second Arcangelo Crisci, the one who married Anna Falco, and it is the pairing with Sara Ruggiero that separates them. Every act above is a **machine transcription of the parish hand and the images are not yet read**, though the 1793 act is attested twice on its own leaf, by the year's index line and by the act.

rows.what: Sweep the MARGINS of every Falco birth act this archive already holds
rows.note:
**Done, and it produced three things.**

**1. Eight citations pointed at the wrong act** — the whole harvest-numbering problem, found because the first act opened was not the act its citation named. Corrected; see row 58 for the 161 never followed.

**2. A marriage nobody would have looked for.** **PASQUA FALCO married PASQUALE CARFORA on 30 December 1880**, written across the foot of her own birth act of 1823. Her second marriage, at fifty-seven, and her first dated sighting after 1856.

**3. THE INSTRUMENT HAS A DATE.** Four acts, sorted by the MARRIAGE: **1844 Raffaele — none. 1845 Crescenzo — none. 1856 Domenico Clemente — annotated. 1880 Pasqua — annotated.** The birth volumes span 1818–1823 and do not predict it; the marriage dates do. **The claim published an hour ago that Luigi Falco's blank margin was «a real negative» is corrected** — the control had not been run. It now means only that he did not marry after about 1855 where Arienzo was told.

rows.what: Settle what «ivi» refers to in these acts — the street, or the comune
rows.note:
**DONE 16 Sep 2026 — «ivi» is the COMUNE, and the finding that rested on it is withdrawn.** The test this row asked for was in three acts already rendered for row 60.

**The proof, three times, in two different printed forms.** The 1824 birth act atto 73 names two witnesses in one sentence: «*Tomaso Esposito … domiciliato **ivi strada Camellara***» and «*Antonio Bernardo … domiciliato **ivi strada Terra Murata***» — one word, two streets. Crescenzo Falco's own 1845 marriage act does it again: groom «*domiciliato **ivi strada Sant'Andrea***», bride «*domiciliata **ivi strada Cappuccini***». And the 1828 death act atto 54 uses «ivi» for the **first** person it names, where the only antecedent is the comune.

**A transcription error was hiding inside it.** The 1845 act reads «domiciliato **ivi** strada Sant'Andrea»; this archive wrote «domiciliato **in** strada Sant'Andrea». Both files are corrected.

**Consequence: a bare «domiciliato ivi» states the comune and gives no street.** So the 1845 act does NOT place Giuseppe Falco off strada Camellara, and the household may never have left. The correction supersedes the published entry; the rest of that finding — Crescenzo's birth date, Antonia di Guida alive in 1845 — is untouched, because it turns on the form marking other parents dead and not these two.

**Written into the method page** as the sixth thing the Arienzo registers taught this archive to distrust, at `/method#ivi`.

rows.what: Identify the twenty-one-row list at the back of the 1819 birth volume
rows.note:
**Done, and the hypothesis it was raised to test is dead.** The same list is at the back of the **1818** volume too — same header «*Nomi, e cognomi de' genitori | Giorno della nascita | Osservazioni*», facing the same 1849 **Procuratore del Re** certificate about counting sheets and removing the blank ones. The «Osservazioni» column carries a roman numeral: **VIII in 1818, XI in 1819**.

**It is NOT a list of births missing from the register.** Its second row in 1818 is «*[Vince]nzo **FALCO** ed Andreana **CRISCI** — **10 Maggio 1818***» — which is **Raffaele Falco, generation four, act 47, folio 149**, sitting in the main sequence at image 42R where it always was. **So it cannot explain Rosaria Falco's absence**, which was the reason for asking.

**What it IS remains open** — the roman numeral and the certificate about removed leaves suggest a reconciliation list for renumbered folios, but that is a guess and is recorded as one.

**What is certain is that it is USABLE.** Parents and a date, one page, at the back of a volume — **and in a year with no annual tavola, such as 1819, it is the only index that exists.** Check the last leaf of every birth volume.

rows.what: A published table of every stated age against its proven date
rows.note:
**Done, and it is on /method.** **VINCENZO FALCO, baptised 1 February 1792**, is the only person in the archive with a proven birth and a long run of civil acts. Six sightings, twelve years: **+10.8, +0.7, −1.9, +0.9, −2.6, −0.9.** **Five of six within three years** — so a stated age here is good to about two or three years and no better, which is now published as the working figure.

**The 1816 outlier is kept**: both spouses inflated by ten years and five in one act, with two readings offered and neither chosen.

**A limit came with it.** It could only be done for one man, because **the archive stores its facts as prose** and the ages sit inside quotations usually attached to somebody else. Any «across all people» question is currently unanswerable here — the same root cause as row 55.

rows.what: The necronyms — the children given a dead sibling's name
rows.note:
**Done, and it found a live conflation instead.** Grouping each household's children by forename turned up the real necronyms — **DOMENICO CLEMENTE** born three days after Domenico was buried, **Giuseppe** and **Mariantonia Cioffi** each given again, **Maddalena the second**, **Matteo the second**, the **first Raffaele of 1816** — and **three pairs that were not necronyms at all but one child spelled two ways.**

**`francesco-cossi` and `francesco-cioffi` were the same man with two pages**, and four children of an established CIOFFI house still carried COSSI. Merged and corrected; **632 people where there were 634.**

**The finding that matters:** in a house that buried six children in nine years **a repeated name is the ordinary case, not the anomaly** — which is exactly why the two living Giovanni were so hard to credit and took weeks.

rows.what: A gate that cross-checks every correction against the data files
rows.note:
**Done, and it is in the build chain as `check:corrections`.** `tools/check_corrections.py` holds two rules.

**First, a table of RETIRED READINGS.** One row per surname a correction has killed, naming the household it was killed in. The gate fails if any PERSON in that household still carries it — while leaving the ACT's own wording alone, because «*GIUSEPPA COSSI, di mesi otto*» is what the clerk actually wrote and must stay quoted.

**Second, no child of one household may appear under two surnames.** Restricted to `role == child` deliberately: a household legitimately holds **Sara Ruggiero the matrina and Sara Falco her granddaughter**, and a gate that flags those is a gate people learn to ignore.

**Tested against the bug it was written for.** Reintroducing «Antonia Cossi» and «Giuseppa Cossi» into the household file makes it fail with three findings and exit 1; the corrected file passes. **It would have caught all three of this week's conflations**, each of which was found by accident.

rows.what: Audit every published COUNT for the living-people zero
rows.note:
**Done. The front-page chart was the only place it had gone wrong, and the reason is worth keeping.** Everything else that displays a total counts a source that already includes the living: the front-page Numbers block counts `people.json`, which holds **all 106 living people** with pages of their own; `/marriages/` counts named and withheld **separately and says so in its dek**; `register.length` counts acts, not people.

**The chart was the one total built from a field that means «publishable».** `n` is `len(g["people"])` in `build_marriedin.py`, and the living never reach that list. **The lesson generalises past this archive**: a count is safe when it is drawn from the population, and dangerous when it is drawn from what the archive is allowed to print about the population.

rows.what: Audit every page that renders text from a JSON data file for raw markdown
rows.note:
**Done. It was on twenty-three more pages.** The built HTML — the only place the fault shows — carried raw markdown on **/worklist (46 backticks), /register (34), /searched (28), /households and /people/crescenzo-falco (13 bold each)** and **nineteen /who/ pages** printing a plate filename in backticks.

**Fixed by one renderer rather than five.** `site/src/lib/md.js` now holds it, `/corrections/` was moved off its private copy onto the shared one, and `/households/`, `/register/`, `/searched/`, `/people/[slug]` and `/who/[slug]` were put on it. Escape first, then render, so no markup inside a transcription can get through.

**/worklist is the exception and it is not this archive's to fix** — see row 17.

rows.what: Check whether /marriages/ carries the same defect the front page did
rows.note:
**Done — and the answer is no, it does not. /marriages/ solved this problem and the chart then reintroduced it.** That page buckets its families three ways: `families` where `n >= 3`, `thin` where `0 < n < 3`, and **`held` where `n === 0`** — and a held family is rendered with its **withheld** count instead of a bar, under a sentence that says it outright: «*Where a family appears with **no named people at all**, every person the archive holds for that surname is living.*»

**So the older page knew.** The shared rule was extracted into `marriedin.js` precisely so the two could not drift — and the chart drifted anyway, by taking `n` from the shared filing and **leaving behind the treatment of zero that was never in the lib.** **Extracting a rule moves the rule, not the knowledge around it.**

rows.what: A person page for every name this archive has only in prose
rows.note:
**Done, and the answer is that the automated version cannot be written — for the same reason row 49's could not.** A regex over the evidence prose returns **268 name-shapes**, and almost all are noise: Latin declensions of people the archive already holds (*Mattheo Falco*, *Vincentium Falco*, *Franciscae Crisci*) and sentence fragments (*comparso Giuseppe Falco*, *two Giuseppe Falco*, *not Cossi*). **The archive stores narrative, and narrative does not yield a list.**

**What the check DID establish is the shape of the leak, and it is not where the row assumed.** Of the candidates, **forty reach the register and are searchable while never becoming a person**; a handful reach neither. The register is the safety net and it usually holds.

**Seven people were promoted by hand** — the ones introduced in the last day and verified individually: Gennaro Morgillo, Maria Felicia Sansone, Angela Maria Morgillo, Domenica Vigliotti, Pasquale Carfora, and the **strada Cossi** household of Francesco Cossi and Teresa Morgillo, which exists to hold the two surnames apart. **638 people.**

rows.what: Re-test the 1841 civil nil now that the two-Giovanni question is settled
rows.note:
**DONE 16 Sep 2026 — THE REGISTER ANSWERS IT ITSELF, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT IT IS NOT CONTINUOUS.**

**Test 1, the numbering gap: there is none.** Acts **78 to 91 run unbroken**, read from the image. And the volume ends at **91**, not ninety — this archive's own statement «*all ninety acts*» was one act short.

**Test 2, a supplementary list at the back: cannot be run on this filming.** There is a tavola leaf after the last act (`an_ua14343` img 55 left), but it is photographed with its ink almost wholly lost and the facing page's writing transferred onto it in mirror. Three order-numbers survive and no names. **Not read, and not recorded as absent.**

**Test 3 is the one that answers the question. THE DEATH DATES HAVE AN ELEVEN-DAY HOLE, AND THE FALCO BURIAL IS INSIDE IT.** Read act by act from the image, the deaths run: **act 84 — 19 November · act 85 — 23 November · act 86 — 26 November · act 87 — 7 DECEMBER.** **The comune registered nothing between 26 November and 7 December 1841. The parish buried JOANNES FALCO on 27 November.**

**And the hole is not special, which is the real finding.** A fortnight earlier the register does it again: **act 80 is a death of 30 October and act 81 a death of 13 November — fourteen days.** Two silences of a fortnight and eleven days in one autumn, in a register that otherwise enters a death every two or three days that season. **This register was not capturing every death at Arienzo**, and its own date sequence proves it without any inference from the parish book.

**So the 1841 civil nil for Falco is not evidence of anything** — and neither is any other nil taken from this volume without checking the dates either side of it. Rows 12 and 56 are the same question and both close here.

rows.what: Re-parse the parish baptism harvest for the child names the parser dropped
rows.note:
**Done — and the row's own premise was wrong, which is the finding.** There is nothing to re-parse. **Every stored transcript is a SNIPPET of at most 260 characters**, and the median length is identical for rows that have a child's name (260) and rows that do not (260). The child column is blank not because a parser gave up but because **the 260-character window happens not to contain the name**. Forty-three of the forty-four blanks are like this.

**A margin-position extractor was written and tried**: eight of forty-four snippets open with a name-shape, and only two are real — **«Cresantios Falco»**, already promoted today, and **«Raphael Falco Obiit die 26 Februarii 1881»**, which is a death annotation rather than a baptism and is now a lead on row 18.

**So the queue is a fetch problem, not a parsing problem.** Forty-three half-answers, each needing the full page or the image. **And the Crescenzo case is explained properly now**: his snippet did contain the name, in the margin position at the very start, which the parser never looked at — it was not defeated by the Latin.

rows.what: Verify that the remaining 171 ANTENATI citations resolve to the acts they name
rows.note:
**Made executable: `tools/citation_check.py`.** **207 citations, and 134 are the SOLE support for their fact** — that is the priority order the row asked for and could not previously produce. Eight are already corrected.

**It prints the render command for each**, so verifying one is a copy and a glance — does the act number match, does the date, is the name there. `--volume an_uaNNNNN` does a whole volume in one sitting, which is the cheap way to spend it: **`an_ua14319` (deaths 1817) alone holds 22 citations, 12 of them sole support.**

**The top of the list is misleading in one way worth knowing**: the acts read from the image in this session sort first because nothing else supports them, and they are verified by construction. **Start at `an_ua14319` and work the old volumes.**

---

**STARTED 20 September — two volumes verified, 35 citations, TWO ERRORS.**

**`an_ua14319` (deaths 1817) — 22 citations across five images, ALL CORRECT.** Including the act this archive is built on: «*RAFFAELE FALCO figlio di VINCENZO FALCO e **ANDREANA CRISCI***», declared 28 October 1817 by **Giuseppe Falco, 37, massaro di campagna, strada Camellara, «PARENTI»**. The name reads **ANDREANA**, not Adriana, which matters given the name-cleaning bug in row 17. One suspicion of mine was **wrong**: «Michedalena Rivetti» looked like it should be «Michela Maddalena», and the act wraps the word across a line break as «MICHE-/DALENA». **The archive's transcription is right and needs no change.**

**`an_ua14318` (deaths 1816) — 13 citations across three images, and two of the three are wrong.**

**1. A citation one leaf early.** Donna Francesca Rivetti's death was cited at **img7L act12**. Image 7 left carries **atto 10**, the death of a Rosa Cimmino. **Act 12 is on img8L** and says exactly what this archive said it says. **The fact was right; the leaf reference was wrong** — the failure mode this row was written to catch.

**2. A month and a mother.** **GAETANA LAUDATO** — «*the deepest this archive reaches*», born about 1738 — was published as dying **9 March 1816** with her mother as «*Giovanna —*», surname unread. **The act reads «a' detto dì NOVE del mese corrente di APRILE» and «figlia delli furono GIACINTO LAUDATO e VITTORIA RUOTOLO».** A month out, and a mother who was never unreadable. Both fixed.

**Method note for whoever continues**: the 22 citations of 1817 sit on **five** images and the 13 of 1816 on **three**. **Render the distinct images, not the citations** — the volume is a few renders, not twenty-two.

**Remaining: `an_ua14416` (13), `an_ua14325` (12), `an_ua14321` (12), `an_ua14320` (12), `an_ua14345` (11)** and the long tail.

**FOUR VOLUMES DONE — 59 citations, FIVE ERRORS, and every error is a DATE or a LEAF, never a fact.**

| volume | citations | images | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `an_ua14319` deaths 1817 | 22 | 5 | **all correct** |
| `an_ua14318` deaths 1816 | 13 | 3 | **2 wrong** |
| `an_ua14320` deaths 1818 | 12 | 4 | **all correct** |
| `an_ua14321` deaths 1819 | 12 | 6 | **2 wrong** |

**1819's two are both off by one day, and both were confirmed at magnification before being touched:**
- **SUOR MARIA MADDALENA RIVETTI** — published **30 March 1819**; the act reads «*a' dì **TRENTUNO** del mese di Marzo*» and repeats «*a' detto dì trentuno … ad ore ventidue*». **31 March.**
- **CARLANTONIO MORGILLO**, declarant — published **20 October 1819**; the act reads «*a' dì **VENTUNO** del mese di Ottobre*». **21 October.** His age series is unaffected.

**THE PATTERN ACROSS ALL FIVE ERRORS IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIXES.** Not one was a misread NAME, a wrong PARENT or an invented RELATIONSHIP. **Every one was a date word or a leaf number** — «trenta» for «trentuno», «venti» for «ventuno», «marzo» for «aprile», img7L for img8L. **The archive reads its people well and its numbers carelessly**, and the small words are exactly what no reader downstream can catch.

**1819 also confirmed the archive's most quoted detail to the hour**: **DOMENICO FALCO** died «*ad ore dodici*» on 15 March and **ROSARIA FALCO** «*ad ore ventitré*» the same day — **eleven hours apart**, as published.

**Remaining: `an_ua14416` (13), `an_ua14325` (12), `an_ua14345` (11)** and the tail.

**`an_ua14416` (births 1819) — 13 citations, the archive's four cornerstone birth acts, and ONE error that could have cost a family.**

**Verified exactly**: **CRESCENZO FALCO**, born 11 October 1819, «*è comparso GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni quaranta, contadino … strada Camellara … da ANTONIA DI GUIDA sua moglie legittima, d'anni trentuno*». **DOMENICO CLEMENTE FALCO**, 18 March 1819, Giuseppe Falco 38, Gelsomina Vigliotta 35 — **and the margin that founded this archive's whole margin method is there and reads as published**: «*Con atto **6 Agosto 1856** atto **21** in **S. Maria a Vico** il Falco sposò **DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI***».

**THE ERROR: Luigi Falco's birth was cited as act 133. It is act 134.** Image 71 left is headed «*Numero d'ordine **CENTOTRENTAQUATTRO***». **And act 133, on the facing leaf, is a different family that looks like this one**: «*è comparso **VINCENZO MAURO**, di anni ventisette, viaticale, strada Sant'Andrea … da **ANDREANA CARFORA** sua moglie legittima, d'anni ventisei, un Maschio*» — **same day, same clerk, a Vincenzo and an Andreana in each.** Anyone chasing act 133 would have found a plausible wrong family. **The leaf reference was right and the number was not.**

**ONE FLAGGED AND DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED.** Act 22 is cited at **19 February 1819** and the date word looks like «*diciotto*» at ordinary magnification. **At the leaf's full resolution it is too faint to separate diciotto from diciannove**, so it stays as published and is recorded here as unresolved. **A date this archive cannot read is not a date it may change.**

**Running total: five volumes, 72 citations, six errors — every one a number, none a person.**

**`an_ua14325` (deaths 1823) — 12 citations, ONE error, and the «nipote» holds.** Act 101 of 9 October 1823 verified word for word: **PAOLO RIVETTI**, fifty, husband of Angela Espositella, of strada Fontana, son of **Pasquale Rivetti defunto** and **Giovanna Perrotta** — declared by **GIOVANNI RIVETTI, twenty-three, POSSIDENTE**, and the relationship word, magnified as this archive's rule requires, is **«Nipote»**. **The error is an age**: Giuseppe Falco fu Matteo is published at forty-three on 20 June 1823 and the act reads **«quarantadue»**. The clerk's own «tre», three lines below on the same leaf, is a different shape.

**`an_ua14345` (deaths 1843) — 11 citations, five acts, THREE errors and all three are dates.** Act 17 is **10 APRIL 1843**, not 10 June: the month is written «Aprile» on both of the act's date lines. Act 29's death is **26 July**, not 27 — the archive had taken the day the act was drawn. Act 33 is **4 AUGUST**, not 14: «il dì quattro del mese di Agosto», and act 32 beside it is 3 August while act 35 is 10 August, so 14 is arithmetically impossible.

**AND THE VOLUME GAVE UP SOMETHING THE ARCHIVE ALREADY OWNED.** Act 33 is **GENNARO MORGILLO**, colono, widower of a Felicia, son of Angelo Morgillo of the Monticello. **Crescenzo Falco married ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO eighteen months later, daughter of a GENNARO MORGILLO DEFUNTO, colono, and of MARIA FELICIA SANSONE defunta.** Two households in this archive, never joined, and the evidence line on one of them called the act «the closest the record comes to the Falco-Morgillo marriage that was still thirty years away». **It was eighteen months away, and the archive held the marriage.** Published as PROBABLE, with the *processetto* named as what would settle it — work-list row 73.

**Running total: seven volumes, 95 citations, ten errors. Not one is a name, a parent or a relationship. Every single one is a number.**

**`an_ua14328` (deaths 1826) — 9 citations, three acts, and THE RULE THIS ROW HAD STARTED TO BELIEVE IS BROKEN.** Act 73 of 28 October is clean: Carlantonio Morgillo and Giuseppe Falco, **both forty-six, both «vicino della Defunta»** — the first act in the series where a Falco and a Morgillo stand side by side, and it verifies exactly. Act 22 of 25 April is right in everything that matters, including the silence: **Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti are named with no «defunto» on a leaf where this scribe does mark the dead.** Its one error is an age — Angelo Sansone is forty-six, not forty-five.

**Act 56 of 9 August gave up TWO MISREAD NAMES, the first of this whole row.** The dead child is **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI**, not Cossi, and his father is **CESARE CIOFFI**, not Gaspare Cossi. **So the finding this row had been repeating — «every error is a number, never a person» — is false, and it is recorded here as false rather than quietly dropped.** Eight volumes, 104 citations, thirteen errors: eleven numbers and two names.

**The same act states a kinship the archive was not holding**: «*SALVATORE SPOSITO … **ZIO DEL DEFUNTO***», the mother's brother, magnified and confirmed. **The 1826 reading log had it all along.**

**And Angelo Sansone's surname settled a question two volumes back.** «Sanſone», in this hand, on this street, is the control that turned the 1843 «Sompone» into **SANSONE** — so the wife of the Gennaro Morgillo who died in 1843 is the **MARIA FELICIA SANSONE** of the 1845 marriage, and the identification of **Crescenzo Falco's father-in-law** now agrees on five things instead of four.

**`an_ua14344` (deaths 1842) and `an_ua14342` (deaths 1840) — 15 citations, seven acts, and the two worst errors of the whole row.**

**1842 is nearly clean.** Act 2 (Luigi Cioffi, one day old, son of Raffaele Cioffi and **FRANCESCA FALCO** — her name plain on the leaf), act 15 (**Don Angelo Scarpati, seventy-six, ARCIPRETE**) and act 80 (Raffaele Cioffi declaring at thirty-six) all verify word for word. **Act 55's first declarant is not a Cioffi**: the Giovanni Cioffi two lines below him carries the double-f ligature and his name does not. It reads **GASPARO**, which is an Arienzo surname — probable, not settled.

**1840 gave up two errors this archive should be ashamed of.**

**One: a quotation that is not in the act.** «*È morta nella sua propria casa MARTA CIOFFI **D'UN MESE***» was published in quotation marks. **The act says «d'anni SETTE».** She was seven years old, not one month. Both declarants were mis-aged with her — Clemente Cioffi is thirty-six, Virgilio Cioffi twenty-three. **A wrong number can be suspected. A quotation cannot.**

**Two: a person who never existed, and a problem invented to go with her.** «**Donna SERAFINA Cimmino**» was published as the mother of the archpriest's sister, with a note calling the 1840/1842 difference «*THE ONE DISCREPANCY, published rather than resolved… either a clerk misread a forename, or Stefano Scarpati married twice*». **Both acts say FAUSTINA.** The misreading was this archive's; the discrepancy was manufactured out of it; and **publishing a doubt is only honest when the doubt is real.** It does buy something back — the archpriest and the sorora now agree on both parents, not one.

**And the age series that was held up as proof of a careful clerk runs backwards.** GIOVANNI CIOFFI was published at «FORTY in 1840, FORTY-SEVEN in August 1842, FORTY-EIGHT in September 1843 — this clerk got one right». **The 1840 act gives him no age at all**, and **the 1843 act says forty-three**, which this archive had read correctly on 15 September and corrected in one file only. **Forty-seven, then forty-three: he got younger.**

**Ten volumes, 119 citations, eighteen errors.** Fourteen numbers, three names, and one sentence that was never written.

**`an_ua14330` (deaths 1828) — 8 citations, four acts, five errors and one act that is perfect.**

**Act 54 is the one that matters and it verifies word for word.** «*Sono comparsi **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di anni **cinquantasei**, di professione **POSSIDENTE**, domiciliato in strada Camellara, **PARENTE DELLA DEFUNTA***» — both the trade and the kinship word magnified. **And the act says it twice**: the second declarant, **CESARE CIOFFI, thirty-one**, of the same street, is «Parente della Defunta» too, which this archive had not recorded.

**Act 11 verifies in everything except the word the household is named after.** Twenty-six months, 14 March, Antonio Morgillo 27 and Simone Morgillo 24 both «parente della defunta» — all right. The mother is **VINCENZA PEPE**, not Vincenza Vece.

**Act 14 and act 56 gave up four numbers and a forename.** The dead boy of May is **PASQUALE**, not Raffaele. **Vincenzo Morgillo is twenty-seven**, not twenty-nine. **Nicola Morgillo is thirty-two**, not thirty-four — and **the act cited for his age does not age him at all**, exactly as with Giovanni Cioffi's «forty in 1840» two volumes ago. **Twice in one morning, a number was attached to a man from an act that never states it.** Vincenzo's wife is **FELICELLA** Rivetti, not Felicetta.

**And the retired reading «Cossi» was still standing in the prose of act 54's evidence**, months after the household was corrected to Cioffi and a gate was written to hold it. **`check_corrections.py` reads person fields, not sentences** — and this archive keeps most of what it knows in sentences.

**Eleven volumes, 127 citations, twenty-three errors.**

**`an_ua14428` (births 1831) — 9 citations, three acts, NOT ONE ERROR.** Aniello Carfora thirty-one and Orsola Porrino thirty on strada Camellara; Raffaele Carfora thirty-seven and Francesca Cioffi twenty-eight; Antonio Carfora twenty-six and Giuseppa Perreca twenty-three on strada Camellara. Every age, every name, every date, both baptism columns: **all of it holds at full resolution.** The first volume of this row to come back clean.

**It gave up three things the archive had not written down.** The acts have numbers — **6, 76 and 85** — and none was recorded. The parish in the second column is **SANT'ANDREA APOSTOLO DI ARIENZO**. And **RAFFAELE CARFORA is on STRADA SIGNORINDICO**, a street this archive's register already knows twenty-three times and which the household's evidence had left off: **he is not on strada Camellara**, where the other two Carfora are. Two Carfora houses on the Falco street and a third elsewhere.

**AND IT NEARLY PRODUCED A FALSE CORRECTION — MINE.** Read down as far as the usual band goes, the baptism column looked like nothing but the printed formula about the parish returning the *notamento*, and the archive's quotation «*il Sacramento del Battesimo è stato amministrato a ANTONIO CARFORA nel giorno dieci Gennajo corrente anno*» looked constructed out of the column's printed heading. **Three quotations were about to be withdrawn as fabrications.** They are all there, lower down the same column, past where the band stopped. **A band is not a page**, and a false correction impugns work that was right — which this archive already knows and had to relearn inside an audit whose whole purpose is not to do that.

**Twelve volumes, 136 citations, twenty-three errors.**

**`an_ua14249` (marriages 1845) — 7 citations, all on one act, and the act is the spine of generation five.** Act 3 of 2 February 1845 verifies almost entirely: **Domenico Zinelli Sindaco**, Arienzo, **distretto di Caserta**, ore ventuno; Crescenzo Falco colono «domiciliato **ivi** strada Sant'Andrea»; **GIUSEPPE FALCO and ANTONIA DI GUIDA both named without «defunto» in an act that writes it twice for the bride's parents**; the church celebration on **3 February** before **LUIGI VERDICCHIO** and **NUNZIO RIVETTI**.

**The one error is a letter, and it undoes a claim.** The bride's mother is **MARIA FELICIA SANSONE**, not Sanzone — a long **ſ**, not a **z**, proved against «Cre**s**cen**z**o» four lines above, whose z has no ascender. **So the surname this archive announced as one that «HAD NEVER APPEARED IN THIS ARCHIVE AT ALL» is one it was already holding**: ANGELO SANSONE, contadino of strada Camellara, declared Maria Falco's death in 1826. **The same wrong letter had been read three ways in three files — Sompone, Sanzone, and nothing.**

**AND A SECOND FALSE CORRECTION WAS AVOIDED IN THE SAME ACT.** The groom is «**maggiore** di anni venticinque», which elsewhere is a statement of legal majority and not of age — on that reading the act bounds his birth on one side only and this archive's «it dates his birth» is false. **The bride, four lines below, is «maggiore di anni VENTITRE», and no age of majority is twenty-three.** «Maggiore» is a status, the number is the age, the inference stands. **Two near-misses in two volumes; both controls were inside the document.**

**Thirteen volumes, 143 citations, twenty-four errors.**

**`an_ua14322` (deaths 1820) — 7 citations, two acts, one wrong number.** **ANNA FALCO's death act verifies word for word**, and it is one of the load-bearing acts of the whole archive: twenty-five, wife of Arcangelo Crisci, «*figlia di **PASCALE FALCO** … e di **CHIARA RIVETTI***», **neither parent marked «defunto»**, declared by two Martone of strada Camellara. **The error is on the other act**: Fortunato Crisci's death is **act 6**, not act 5 — **and the trap is the volume's own layout, because the stamped figure in the margin is the FOLIO**. Folio 5 carries act 6; folio 25 carries act 47.

**`an_ua14421` (births 1824) — 7 citations, three acts, NOT ONE ERROR.** Even the folio stamps this archive recorded — 139, 134, 181 — are right. **The second clean volume of the row.**

**But it had been read three times and not read.** Act 26 was cited here for the child, for the father and for the date, and the same sentence says «*che lo stesso è nato da **ANTONIA DI GUIDA** sua moglie legittima, **di anni QUARANTA***». **This archive held no age at all for her** — generation four's wife, whose death has never been found and whose last dated sighting is 1845. **Forty in March 1824, so born about 1784, and about sixty-one at her son's wedding.**

**That is the finding of these two volumes, and it is not an error.** A citation verified is not a document read, and **the commonest thing this row has turned up is not a wrong word but an unread one.**

**Fifteen volumes, 157 citations, twenty-five errors.**

**`an_ua14264` (marriages 1860) — 6 citations, one act, and it is the best thing this row has found.** The act is the marriage of **SABBATINO ANNECCHINO of Forchia** to **MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA of Arienzo**, 21 January 1860 — **the spine of the Annecchino line this family descends from**.

**A LIVING MAN HAD BEEN BURIED BY A QUOTATION.** This archive published «*fu CARMINE ANNECCHINO … fu ROSA CEGLIA … fu [?]ERIO CARFORA … fu PASQUA MORGILLO*», four «fu» inside quotation marks. **The act uses «fu» nowhere.** It writes «defunto» and «defunta» after the name, and **it writes them three times, not four**: the bride's father is «*di professione contadino, domiciliato **ivi***» **and nothing else**. **He was alive.** The act says so again in its own list of documents — item **6** is «*Nel **CONSENSO DEL PADRE** della stessa, **dato nell'atto***».

**AND THE NAME WAS NEVER ILLEGIBLE. IT WAS SPLIT.** This archive recorded that «*the word reads «[L/t]erio» at four times magnification and is left unread rather than guessed*». **The word is two half-words**: the line ends «*figlia di **Va***» and the next begins «***lerio** Carfora*». **VALERIO CARFORA** — and no Italian forename ends in *-lerio* except that one. **A good rule was applied to the wrong object: the archive magnified the second half of a word and called the whole of it unreadable.**

**The act also lists the eight documents it was built on, and item 4 is a GENERATION**: «*Nell'atto di morte dell'**AVO PATERNO** dello stesso*» — the groom's paternal grandfather, the father of Carmine Annecchino, **a man this archive has never named**. That is work-list row 77.

**Also: the act is of the twenty-first, not the twentieth; the groom writes SABBATINO with two b; and the witness is CRISCI, not Crispi.**

**Sixteen volumes, 163 citations, twenty-nine errors.**

**`an_ua14323` (deaths 1821) — 6 citations, one act, one error.** Carmine Rivetti, fifty-three, husband of Giustina Morgillo, «*figlio di **NICOLA RIVETTI Defunto** … e di **ANNA DI RUGGIO Defunta***» — the act that gave this archive its best candidate for Chiara Rivetti's parents — **verifies exactly**. The error is the second declarant's patronymic: **GIOVANNI MORGILLO fu PASCALE**, not «fu Raffaele». **And the act is the proof of the rule this archive broke eleven volumes later**: «fu» here is a **patronymic on a living man**, while the death mark in the filiation clause is «**Defunto**» AFTER the name — written twice on this very leaf.

**`an_ua14327` (deaths 1825) — 6 citations, three acts, NOT ONE ERROR.** Maddalena Falco at seven; Giuseppa Cioffi at eight months; **CLEMENTE FALCO at fifteen months, and the arithmetic closes to the day** against his birth act of 11 March 1824. **The third clean volume.** It gives up an act number nobody recorded — Clemente's death is **atto 34** — and **CESARE CIOFFI, thirty, of strada Camellara**, which independently corroborates the «Cesare Cioffi» read out of the 1826 volume this morning.

**And it hands over a second demonstration that the ages are guessed, sharper than the archive's own.** **ANIELLO DIGLIO is forty-six on 2 April 1825 and FIFTY on 19 June 1825** — four years in seventy-eight days, beside Giuseppe Falco's five years in four days. **Two men, two pairs of acts, one volume.**

**Eighteen volumes, 175 citations, thirty errors.**

**`an_ua14071` (Diversi 1825) — 9 citations, one act, and the act had two men standing in its first line that nobody had written down.** Everything this archive took off the leaf about the dead man verifies: **CRESCENZO CRISCI, fifty-three, colono, husband of ANGELA QUOTOLO, dead in the Masseria di Domenico de Luca at the luogo FABRICA**, son of **ALESSANDRO CRISCI Defunto** and **CARMINA SORRINO**, leaving **Aniello fifteen, Sante twelve, Carmina ten** — all exact.

**The declarants are his BROTHERS.** «*sono comparsi **DOMENICO CRISCI GERMANO DEL DEFUNTO**, d'anni quarantanove, colono … e **GABRIELE CRISCI GERMANO***». **«Germano» is full brother**, magnified before it was written down. So Alessandro Crisci and Carmina Sorrino had **at least three sons**, and this archive had one of them. **The act was read for the family it buried and not for the family it named.**

**The youngest child is MARIA, not «Maria Rosa».** The clerk closes the list by giving the last child the family surname — «*e **Maria Crisci** d'anni cinque*» — and the surname was read as a forename. **A child filed under a name she never had is a child no index will return.**

**AND GABRIELE'S AGE IS NOT PUBLISHED, BECAUSE IT CANNOT BE READ.** His line runs into the binding, which on this filming is in shadow. **A first pass over this page had «d'anni trentuno» for him; that was the reader's eye filling a gap and it is not in the image.** The near-miss is recorded because **the gutter shadow is exactly where this archive will invent something if it is not careful.**

**Nineteen volumes, 184 citations, thirty-two errors.**

**`an_ua14326` (deaths 1824) — 5 citations, two acts, one unresolved word improved.** The act this archive once had to correct verifies completely: «*PASCALE FALCO, di anni cinquantacinque, **COLONO** … **ZIO DEL DEFUNTO**, e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni quarantadue, colono … **ZIO DEL DEFUNTO***» — **both «zio», both magnified, both right** — and so does the child they buried, **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI, five years old**, son of Francesco Cioffi and Maria Falco. **Donn'Anna Quotolo's mother is NOT «d'Isteria»**: the word ends **-ustina** with no **r**, and reads most likely **DI GIUSTINA**. The negative is settled; the positive is not.

**`an_ua14334` (deaths 1832) — 5 citations and FIVE ERRORS. The worst volume of the row, and the only one where every citation failed.** **Both image references point at other families**: image 20 left is act 30, **Michele Morgillo son of Nicola Morgillo and Elisabetta Crisci**; image 48 right is act 79, **DON FRANCESCANTONIO GESSI, seventy-eight, PROPRIETARIO**. Act 32 is on **image 21 left**; Carmina Falco is **act 81 on image 49 right**.

**And the readings were a decade and a name out.** **GIOVANNA FALCO is SESSANTA, not settanta** — «*ſeſſanta*», two long ſ and no crossed tt — so born about **1772**, not 1762. Her husband is **ANTONIO LETTIERI**, not «Antonio Sett[embre]». Her mother is **VINCENZA SPOSITO**, not Esposito.

**The evidence for this volume is five terse unformatted lines with no quotation and no act cited in the original.** **It was harvested and never read**, and it is the only volume in twenty-one where that shows in every single line.

**Twenty-one volumes, 194 citations, thirty-eight errors.**

**`an_ua14336` (deaths 1834) — 5 citations, FOUR of them wrong, and one of them is withdrawn outright.**

**The act that matters most is right.** **PASCALE FALCO, seventy-four, husband of CHIARA RIVETTI, son of MATTEO FALCO Defunto and FRANCESCA CRISCI Defunta**, dead on 1 October 1834 — **act 69, verified word for word**. Only the half of the leaf was missing from the citation, and image 43 LEFT is a Nicola Rivetti a reader would have landed on.

**MARIA ROSA FALCO WAS TWENTY-TWO MONTHS OLD, NOT SIXTEEN YEARS.** «*di **mesi** ventidue*», magnified. Everything anyone might have built on «sedici» — a birth about 1818, a working girl, a marriageable daughter — **was wrong in the direction that invites false matches.** Her mother, **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, had never been recorded, and she opens a real question against the **ANTONIA MIGLIORE** married to a Michele Falco in 1842.

**The infant PASCALE FALCO of December 1834 is act 89 on image 54 right**, not image 53 right — which is Maria Michele Sperato — **and his mother ANDREANA CRISCI was in the act and not on the page**.

**AND ONE CITATION IS WITHDRAWN.** «Anna Falco, eight days old, daughter of MICHELANGELO FALCO, 7 March 1834» cites image 10 left. **Image 10 left is MARIA PORRINO, eight days old, dead on the 8th of March.** Five leaves around it were opened and hold no Falco; **MICHELANGELO FALCO is a forename that appears nowhere else in this archive**; and **she is entered twice**, so she has been counted twice in every Falco total this archive publishes. **The person is not deleted and the citation is** — row 78.

**Row 62 found the seam; this row works it.** FamilySearch collection **`2043630`** holds **202 distinct Arienzo pages** naming a Falco, 1891–1910, and their certified extracts quote Arienzo civil acts from years Antenati does not hold. **One pass on one surname recovered seventeen.**

**1. Read the images.** Every extract in `notes/arienzo-1866-1890-via-processetti.md` carries its ark. **A machine transcription is a candidate and nothing more** — the OCR renders Arienzo as «Chienno», «Criengo» and «Artento» on the same pages.
